moments.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh
SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: Two baskets of figs before the temple after Jeconiah was carried to Babylon: one very good, the other so naughty they could not be eaten.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The good figs are the righteous people carried captive whom the Lord acknowledges for their good: he will bring them again, build and not pull down, plant and not pluck up, and give them a heart to know him because they return with their whole heart.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: The evil figs are Zedekiah, his princes and those left in the land and in Egypt, delivered to be a reproach and a curse in every kingdom with sword, famine and pestilence. Good fig or bad fig is your decision.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Jeremiah is making a comparison: one basket had very good figs, and the other basket had very naughty figs, spoiled figs.
Why is Zedekiah mentioned? Because he resisted Nebuchadnezzar. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed his family and took his eyes out; he suffered much pain because he was resisting the hand of God.

Them that dwell in the land of Egypt: although our people ran into Egypt they could not escape the hand of God; Nebuchadnezzar came against Egypt and destroyed it. Some of them stayed there, some migrated further down into Upper Egypt, some went into Libya and other parts of the continent of Africa. Our people always ran into Egypt seeking refuge.
The Most High shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs set before the temple after Nebuchadnezzar had carried Jeconiah, the princes of Judah, the carpenters, and the smiths away captive to Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: One basket held very good figs like the first ripe, and the other held very naughty figs so bad they could not be eaten; the baskets represent the house of Israel.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: Like the good figs, the Most High will acknowledge them that are carried away captive into the land of the Chaldeans for their good, to set His eyes upon them, bring them again to this land, build them, and plant them.

There were good Israelites among us who had to suffer with the bad; some of our people, like Daniel and the three Hebrew boys called Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego by their Babylonian names, were kept in captivity for their good.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: He will give them a heart to know Him, and they shall be His people and return unto Him with their whole heart.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: Like the evil figs that cannot be eaten, so the Most High will give up Zedekiah, his princes, and the residue of Jerusalem, including them that dwell in Egypt, to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth for their hurt.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: They become a reproach, a proverb, a taunt, and a curse in every place, and He sends the sword, the famine, and the pestilence among them until they are consumed; sin took over everybody and the whole nation went into captivity, some there for their good and others for raw servitude and punishment.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: The Most High gives Jeremiah a parable to tell Israel. “The Lord shewed me, and, behold, two baskets of figs were set before the temple of the Lord”, after Nebuchadrezzar had carried away captive Jeconiah king of Judah, with “the princes of Judah, with the carpenters and smiths, from Jerusalem”.
Jeconiah was another king of Judah, and he went by more than one name. He ruled real briefly, about three months, and he was dethroned by the king of Babylon. That is just to give you the history.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “One basket had very good figs, even like the figs that are first ripe: and the other basket had very naughty figs, which could not be eaten, they were so bad.” The Lord asks Jeremiah what he sees: “Figs; the good figs, very good; and the evil, very evil, that cannot be eaten, they are so evil.”

When you read on down, he gives the example of the other figs, the evil and naughty ones. These are the Israelites that rebelled against Babylon, that did not listen to Jeremiah, and guess who is in this bunch: Zedekiah.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “Like these good figs, so will I acknowledge them that are carried away captive of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans for their good.” Carried away for their good means the Most High showed mercy to these Israelites. This is Daniel, this is Ezekiel, these are the other captives that were taken out of the land for their good.
It shows you the Most High had mercy on some of our people that were enslaved. He shows mercy to some, and to others he does not show mercy.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “For I will set mine eyes upon them for good, and I will bring them again to this land: and I will build them, and not pull them down; and I will plant them, and not pluck them up.” And he will give them “an heart to know me, that I am the Lord: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.”

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “For I will set mine eyes upon them for good”: he is setting his eyes upon the Israelites for good, that’s us. “And I will bring them again to this land”: so America is not our final destination. “And I will build them, and not pull them down”: God said he will build us and not pull us down. “And I will plant them, and not pluck them up.”

“And I will give them an heart to know me”: he is going to change our mind. That is what is going on now; he is changing the way we think, the way we act, the way we talk. “That I am the Lord: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.” That is the prophecy we are in the midst of right now.
